headline: DMP probe into State Minister Ishraque's use of firearms during anti-drug drive
summary: The Dhaka Metropolitan Police have ordered an investigation after videos showed State Minister Ishraque Hossain brandishing a gun during an operation in Gandaria.
details: The Dhaka Metropolitan Police (DMP) has ordered an investigation into State Minister for Liberation War Affairs Ishraque Hossain brandishing firearms during an 'anti-drug operation'.
The investigation was triggered by videos uploaded to the minister's own verified Facebook page, showing him and associates chasing people in Gandaria.
In the footage, Ishraque and another individual are seen carrying firearms while pursuing a group of people during the drive.
State Minister Ishraque Hossain explained that he drew his licensed gun in 'self-defence' during the operation.
DMP Detective Branch chief Shafiqul Islam stated that the deputy commissioner of the DMP’s Wari Division has been assigned to the probe.
The police chief added that legal action will be taken if any violation of the law is found during the investigation.
caption:
A State Minister brandishing a gun during a 'drug raid'? DMP orders a probe.

The Dhaka Metropolitan Police (DMP) has ordered an investigation into State Minister for Liberation War Affairs Ishraque Hossain brandishing firearms during an 'anti-drug operation'.

The investigation was triggered by videos uploaded to the minister's own verified Facebook page, showing him and associates chasing people in Gandaria.

In the footage, Ishraque and another individual are seen carrying firearms while pursuing a group of people during the drive.

State Minister Ishraque Hossain explained that he drew his licensed gun in 'self-defence' during the operation.

DMP Detective Branch chief Shafiqul Islam stated that the deputy commissioner of the DMP’s Wari Division has been assigned to the probe.

The police chief added that legal action will be taken if any violation of the law is found during the investigation.

headline_marked: 10 killed in Cox's Bazar fire: [[Police sue resort owner]] and manager
headline: 10 killed in Cox's Bazar fire: Police sue resort owner and manager
summary: A case has been filed against the owner of Tup-Tup Resort in Inani, where a devastating fire claimed 10 lives. The resort manager has been arrested.
details: A devastating fire at the Tup-Tup Resort in Inani, Cox's Bazar, has left 10 people dead. Police have filed a case against the resort's owner, Tanvir, as the primary accused.
The case names 23 people in total, including the owner, four other named individuals and 19 unidentified persons. The resort manager has already been arrested in connection with the case.

Complications have arisen in identifying the victims. The district administration provided a list of 10 deceased persons on Saturday, but a family from Jessore claimed four of their members were among the victims.
The family from Jessore claims that Afsana Motin Tanzi, Nahidur Rahman, Ruzaina Inaya, and Sunaina Ihana died in the fire. However, their names do not match the administration's list.
Due to these discrepancies, the district administration has announced that bodies will be handed over to families only after DNA tests are conducted to ensure correct identification.
Ukhia Police Station's Officer-in-Charge, Atiqur Rahman, stated that operations are ongoing to arrest the remaining accused persons named in the case.
caption:
10 people died in a resort fire in Cox's Bazar. Now, the owner and 22 others are facing criminal charges.

A devastating fire at the Tup-Tup Resort in Inani, Cox's Bazar, has left 10 people dead. Police have filed a case against the resort's owner, Tanvir, as the primary accused.

The case names 23 people in total, including the owner, four other named individuals and 19 unidentified persons. The resort manager has already been arrested in connection with the case.

Complications have arisen in identifying the victims. The district administration provided a list of 10 deceased persons on Saturday, but a family from Jessore claimed four of their members were among the victims.

The family from Jessore claims that Afsana Motin Tanzi, Nahidur Rahman, Ruzaina Inaya, and Sunaina Ihana died in the fire. However, their names do not match the administration's list.

Due to these discrepancies, the district administration has announced that bodies will be handed over to families only after DNA tests are conducted to ensure correct identification.

Ukhia Police Station's Officer-in-Charge, Atiqur Rahman, stated that operations are ongoing to arrest the remaining accused persons named in the case.

Source: Jamuna TV, Dhaka Tribune, The Daily Star, Prothom Alo
